text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening stance and repeated first-person claims","quality":"positioning","description":"It states a definite position on driverless cars and keeps that stance visible throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"explains convenience, safety, and moral concerns in separate paragraphs","quality":"organization","description":"It groups ideas into a recognizable introduction, body, and conclusion with clearer paragraph-level structure."},{"evidence":"“safe they are… tested more” and “A computer wont figure out those kinds of morals”","quality":"reasoning","description":"It develops its argument with explanations of why the technology should be limited, not just with opinions."},{"evidence":"references to picking people up, getting more done, and life-threatening decisions","quality":"support development","description":"It expands points with concrete examples that make the argument feel more fully developed."},{"evidence":"“What will the vehicle decide on what to do?” and “If we can make self driving vehicles, what are the other possibilities”","quality":"rhetorical engagement","description":"It uses rhetorical questions and direct appeals to engage the reader and emphasize key concerns."},{"evidence":"“Then again,” “Also,” “What if”","quality":"transitional flow","description":"It uses simple linking language to move between ideas more smoothly than the other essay."}]}
